verified.claim: NOTICE.md states 'The full upstream MIT license text is preserved in `poc/qure_compliance/LICENSE`' but no `LICENSE` file appears anywhere under `poc/qure_compliance/` in the file listing.
verified.evidence: The full upstream MIT license text is preserved in `poc/qure_compliance/LICENSE`.
verified.why_it_matters: The attribution obligation from the upstream MIT-licensed code (claude-video-vision) cannot be verified or fulfilled if the LICENSE file does not exist, creating a compliance gap between the stated and actual state of the repository.
verified.verifier_note: Legal/attribution gap with explicit textual claim vs. absent file — high-impact and easy for a reviewer to verify.

verified.claim: The smoke test asserts three registered MCP tools — `compliance_scan`, `video_info`, and `video_setup` — but only `compliance_scan` has a corresponding source file in the repository; `src/tools/video_info.ts` and `src/tools/video_setup.ts` are absent from the file listing.
verified.why_it_matters: The smoke test will exit 1 on every run because two of the three tools it expects cannot exist without their source files, meaning `npm run smoke` is broken and the claimed tool surface area is fiction.
verified.verifier_note: Tools may be registered inline in a server file rather than as separate source files, but the absence of the files combined with the hard assertion is concrete enough to flag — reviewer should confirm registration site.

verified.claim: The transcript extraction script references `evals/golden/v1.1.0/videos/` as its video source directory, but no `videos/` subdirectory exists under `evals/golden/v1.1.0/` in the file listing.
verified.why_it_matters: The script will silently skip all 10 videos with 'video not found' messages and produce no transcripts, making the golden-set preparation workflow non-functional without any obvious error to a new contributor.
verified.verifier_note: Concrete missing-directory claim that breaks the documented golden-set workflow; videos directories are often gitignored but the script's silent-skip behavior is the real defect.

verified.claim: The eval README documents that `runner.ts` reads video files from `../../../evals/golden/v1.0.0/videos/*.mp4`, but no `videos/` subdirectory exists under `evals/golden/v1.0.0/` or `evals/golden/v1.1.0/` in the file listing.
verified.why_it_matters: Anyone following the documented eval workflow will encounter a missing-file error immediately; the golden set videos are either never downloaded or the download script's output path diverged from what the runner expects.
verified.verifier_note: Video binaries are typically gitignored, so absence is expected, but the README should explicitly say so — keep as a documentation/UX defect rather than a true correctness bug.

verified.claim: EXISTING_G001 is a hardcoded absolute-style relative path pointing to a specific dated audit output directory that is unlikely to exist in other developer environments or CI.
verified.why_it_matters: The path encodes a specific run timestamp; on any other machine or after audit output is cleaned, os.path.exists returns False and the script prints 'video not found' for g001, producing a silently incomplete golden set that skews eval metrics.
verified.verifier_note: Hardcoded timestamped path is a clear reproducibility defect for the golden-set build pipeline.

verified.claim: The fallback branch silently returns a video-only (no audio) file when yt-dlp produces per-stream fragments but no merged output, without throwing or logging a warning that audio-dependent criteria (C6, C7) will silently fail.
verified.why_it_matters: Downstream transcript-based rubric criteria (C6, C7) are hard_fail criteria; silently processing a muted file will produce systematically wrong verdicts without any indication of the root cause.
verified.verifier_note: The inline comment itself acknowledges the silent failure mode — downgraded from P0 to P1 because impact depends on rare yt-dlp output state and the comment shows the author is aware.

verified.claim: requireAnthropicKey's placeholder guard `k.startsWith("sk-ant-...")` only catches the literal placeholder substring, providing no structural validation beyond a 10-char length check; misconfigured keys can pass.
verified.why_it_matters: The guard gives false confidence that a real key is present; a fabricated 10-char string passes startup validation and is forwarded to the live API, obscuring configuration errors at runtime.
verified.verifier_note: Real defect but P0 overstates it — invalid keys still fail at the API call boundary; downgrading and consolidating with the duplicate Finding 15.

verified.claim: writeAuditJson performs an atomic write via temp+rename but does not clean up the .tmp file on failure, leaving orphaned temporary files.
verified.why_it_matters: If writeFile succeeds but rename fails, the .tmp file persists and may be mistaken for a valid audit file by directory-listing logic in nextAuditId.
verified.verifier_note: Real robustness gap in atomic-write pattern; the directory-listing collision risk only materializes if readdir doesn't filter by suffix, which reviewer can verify.

verified.claim: The vision_model default is hardcoded to 'claude-sonnet-4-6', which does not correspond to any publicly documented Anthropic model identifier.
verified.why_it_matters: A wrong default model ID causes every production scan that doesn't override QURE_VISION_MODEL to fail or be routed to an unintended model, with no startup validation.
verified.verifier_note: Model ID looks malformed (Anthropic uses formats like `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`); worth surfacing for the reviewer to confirm.

verified.claim: The audit record persists `models_used` with optional `snapshot` field but does not capture the raw prompt text sent to the model.
verified.evidence: models_used: input.modelsUsed, ... typed as `Array<{ role: string; model_id: string; snapshot?: string }>` — no prompt or raw-response field is present in `SerializeInput`.
verified.why_it_matters: Without persisting the exact prompt, a future auditor cannot verify the model was queried under the rubric version active at the time, nor reproduce the inference.
verified.verifier_note: Valid governance/reproducibility concern for an audit-trail system; severity appropriately P2 since prompts can be reconstructed from code+rubric version.

verified.claim: The thresholds `max_frames: 120` and `target_fps: 0.5` are hardcoded defaults with no inline citation to the rubric file, spec document, or evaluation result that justifies those values.
verified.why_it_matters: Threshold defaults without cited rationale cannot be defended to a regulator; overrides via env vars also lack range validation.
verified.verifier_note: Reasonable governance flag for a compliance-audit tool where defensibility of magic numbers matters.

verified.claim: No `.env.example` file appears in the 116-file listing, even though `config.ts` references at least six environment variables that operators must supply.
verified.evidence: config.ts L44: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ... L50: OPENAI_API_KEY ... no `.env.example` file appears in the repository listing.
verified.why_it_matters: Without a `.env.example`, a new operator cannot determine the full set of required secrets without reading source code, increasing misconfiguration risk.
verified.verifier_note: Standard onboarding/operability gap; P2 is appropriate.

verified.claim: The module docstring references 'poc/base/mcp-server/src/backends/local.ts' but no `poc/base/` directory exists in the repository.
verified.evidence: Pattern adapted from poc/base/mcp-server/src/backends/local.ts (MIT, Jordan Vasconcelos).
verified.why_it_matters: The referenced upstream file path is a stale attribution that cannot be verified within the repository.
verified.verifier_note: Provenance comment likely references a sibling repo not in this checkout; minor but worth fixing for attribution clarity.

verified.claim: `package.json` declares version `0.1.0` while `dashboard/index.html` displays `v1.1.0` and eval golden sets are `v1.0.0`/`v1.1.0`, creating an inconsistent version narrative.
verified.evidence: package.json: "version": "0.1.0" / dashboard/index.html: "v1.1.0 short-form golden set · 10 videos"
verified.why_it_matters: A reader cannot determine whether `0.1.0` pre-dates `v1.0.0` eval or is a separate versioning axis, creating confusion about which software version produced published eval results.
verified.verifier_note: Software version vs. rubric/eval version are legitimately separate axes, but the docs don't say so — minor clarity gap.

verified.claim: rootDir is './src' but tests/ and evals/ are excluded from compilation, so type errors in test utilities are not surfaced by tsc.
verified.why_it_matters: Test files import from src under strict mode assumptions but are never type-checked by tsc; type regressions go undetected until vitest runtime.
verified.verifier_note: Common TS project pattern; vitest does type-check via tsx, so impact is modest but the gap is real.

rejected.claim: nextAuditId catches readdir errors and silently swallows them with a comment 'dir didn't exist', but mkdir with recursive:true on line L105 already creates the directory, so the catch block is dead code that also hides real I/O errors.
rejected.reason: The catch is defensive against TOCTOU and non-ENOENT errors (e.g., EACCES post-mkdir); calling it 'dead code' is incorrect, and the duplicate-ID risk is speculative — reviewer noise outweighs signal.

rejected.claim: scripts/scan-secrets.sh exits 0 silently when both stdin and TOOL_INPUT are empty, providing no defence when invoked outside the expected hook context.
rejected.reason: Exit 0 on empty input is correct hook behavior — there is nothing to scan; flagging this as a security gap misreads the script's contract.

rejected.claim: ModelCall and Trace are imported from types.ts but ModelCall is never referenced in this file's code.
rejected.reason: Unused-import nitpick; TS compiler/linter handles this and it does not warrant audit-report space.

rejected.claim: The rubric file name encodes 'v1' but the file itself was not sampled, so it is unconfirmed whether a machine-readable `version` field exists inside the JSON.
rejected.reason: Speculative finding admitting the evidence was not examined; the cited loader test (`expect(r.version).toBe("1.0.0")`) actually confirms the field exists and is read.

rejected.claim: The compliance rubric documentation file was not sampled; it cannot be confirmed whether it carries a `version` field or change-log.
rejected.reason: Pure speculation based on not having read the file — not a defensible audit finding.

rejected.claim: Duplicate of placeholder-key guard finding (governance P2 version covering config.ts L44-L48).
rejected.reason: Duplicates Finding 1/15 already kept once at P1; suppressing the duplicate per dedup rule.

rejected.claim: The transcript-extraction script hardcodes a path to a specific prior audit output as a production data source for g001, creating an undocumented dependency on a local artifact.
rejected.reason: Duplicates Finding 4 (same file/line/issue) already kept under code_quality lens.

rejected.claim: tsconfig sets rootDir to ./src and outDir to ./dist, yet evals/README.md instructs users to run `node dist/evals/runner.js` — evals/ sits outside src/ and would not be compiled.
rejected.reason: Could not verify the README instruction text from cited evidence; the runner may live at src/evals/runner.ts and emit to dist/evals/, which is consistent with the config. Insufficient evidence to ship.

rejected.claim: The vision client (`src/vision/client.ts`) has no corresponding test file under `tests/vision/`, while every other src/ subdirectory has matching tests.
rejected.reason: Absence-of-test observation is structural commentary, not a defect with concrete evidence of a regression; risk of false-positive noise in audit report.

rejected.claim: Neither `src/backends/transcription.ts` nor `src/extractors/ffmpeg.ts` nor `src/extractors/source.ts` has a corresponding test file, despite being adapted from upstream MIT code.
rejected.reason: Subprocess-wrapping code is notoriously hard to unit-test and is typically covered by smoke/integration tests; flagging coverage gaps without evidence of a defect is speculative.
